What it is: Sequence is an architecture inspection tool for software repositories.
Who it is for: developers and team leads who want to verify the mapping between code and structure.
Why it exists: to keep an architecture graph honest as code changes, with real edges traceable to imports rather than assumptions.
How it works:
1. The tool reads the repository into a live architecture graph using static analysis.
2. Edges on the board are backed by real imports, calls, routes, or manifest lines.
3. Any proposed or drawn edge stays dashed until the scanner finds it in code.
4. The tool runs locally with no external data leaving the machine.
5. Chat on the right answers questions from the scanned graph and cites evidence.
Advantages: it gives teams a verifiable architecture view without manual diagramming, ensures trust in discovered connections, and keeps the graph accurate as code evolves.
